prompt: In $4\text{NH}_3+5\text{O}_2\to4\text{NO}+6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, how many moles of oxygen react with 2.0 mol of ammonia?
25.0 cm³ of NaOH solution is neutralised by 18.5 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄. Calculate the concentration of the NaOH.

5.00 g of magnesium is added to 100 cm³ of 1.00 mol dm⁻³ HCl. $\text{Mg}+2\text{HCl}\to\text{MgCl}_2+\text{H}_2$

**(a)** Determine the limiting reactant. **[2]**

**(b)** Calculate the theoretical volume of hydrogen at STP (22.7 dm³ mol⁻¹). **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $n(\text{Mg})=\dfrac{5.00}{24.31}=0.206$ mol, which needs 0.411 mol HCl; only 0.100 mol HCl is present, so HCl is limiting **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** $n(\text{H}_2)=0.0500$ mol **(A1)**; $V=1.14\ \text{dm}^{3}$ **(A1)**

prompt: The theoretical yield of hydrogen in an experiment is 1.14 dm³, but 1.02 dm³ is collected. Calculate the percentage yield and suggest one reason it is below 100%.
markscheme: $\dfrac{1.02}{1.14}\times100=89.5\%$ **(A1)**; e.g. gas escaped before the stopper was fitted, or some dissolved in the water **(A1)**

prompt: Ethanol can be made by fermentation, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\to2\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}+2\text{CO}_2$, or by hydration of ethene, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4+\text{H}_2\text{O}\to\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$. Calculate the atom economy of each and comment. ($M$: glucose 180.18, ethanol 46.08)
markscheme:
Fermentation: $\dfrac{2\times46.08}{180.18}\times100=51.1\%$ **(A1)**; hydration: 100% (one product) **(A1)**

Hydration wastes no atoms, but uses ethene from crude oil; fermentation uses a renewable feedstock **(R1)**
